rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This experiment tests a simple RNA-only model with PCA encoding, which isolates the RNA modality's performance. It clarifies the baseline accuracy and helps identify if multimodal approaches provide incremental value, aligning with the principle of reducing uncertainty about critical design choices.

The existing evidence shows that rna_only with singleprofile and pca_n2000 achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, clarifying whether multiprofile settings and aggregation methods improve performance. It isolates the effect of profile settings and aggregation, a key design choice, while keeping RNA encoder and fusion unchanged.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile models. This experiment tests whether changing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping aggregation as avgpool) improves accuracy, isolating the effect of representation choice. This balances exploration of promising design choices with exploitation of the multiprofile advantage.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 encoder achieve the highest accuracy (0.650124). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_005) with transformer aggregation could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the promising scvi_n200 encoder with exploration of a more complex aggregation strategy, while keeping other parameters consistent.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation achieve the highest accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests whether combining this RNA setup with image data (resnet50) and transformer aggregation (a promising RNA-only method) improves performance. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion (concat) while leveraging prior success with scvi_n200 and transformer, balancing exploitation of strong signals with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_038) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.721). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted in the same configuration improves accuracy, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the remaining budget as it directly builds on the strongest prior result and explores a critical design choice with minimal additional complexity.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) in the same multimodal setup can further improve performance. It directly addresses the uncertainty around the optimal RNA encoder for multimodal tasks and builds on the successful aggregation/fusion strategy from the top-performing config_039.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt while keeping the same aggregation and fusion methods could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, and directly compares against the current best configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.7249). This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA with resnet50 image encoder, which could clarify if the image encoder choice (resnet50 vs. imagenet_vit_l) impacts performance. It balances exploration of image encoder alternatives while maintaining the high-performing scvi_n200 RNA and transformer aggregation, maximizing the chance to find a slightly better configuration within the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders, combined with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039), achieve the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests scgpt RNA with the same image encoder and aggregation but uses concat fusion instead of weighted. It clarifies whether concat fusion could improve performance when paired with scgpt, despite scvi_n200's prior superiority. This is the final opportunity to explore a critical design choice (fusion method) in a high-performing multimodal setup.
